newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific leaks flood out from Canberra.
newsitem.headline: Pacific leaks flood out from Canberra.

text.p: Australia, already embarrassed by the loss of a top secret paper slating its Pacific neighbours, faced further discomfort on Wednesday with more leaks, including an angry diplomatic e-mail.

As international criticism continued over the first gaffe, the leaked foreign affairs department memo criticised "securocrats" in Prime Minister John Howard's intelligence office for believing in "a darker reality".

The government on Wednesday widened an inquiry into Reuters' publication last week of a 93-page AUSTEO -- Australian Eyes Only -- paper which contained a scathing assessment of South Pacific economies and leaders. The inquiry will now include a second AUSTEO paper published on Wednesday.

A third document has also leaked out, a diplomatic memo criticising Howard's Office of National Assessments' scathing rundown on the Pacific. It was stapled to notes given to journalists at a briefing on another issue.

"The fundamental problem seems to be that assessment agencies are disdainful of reality as presented by those of us out in the field and convinced that there is some darker reality which only they, from their securocrats' ivory tower, can detect and on which, as they jump at shadows, they insist on having the last word," said the memo from Ian Lincoln, dated Wednesday.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade lists Ian Lincoln as Australia's deputy high commissioner to New Zealand. A department spokeswoman told Reuters she could not comment on what appeared to be private correspondence between two people.

The second AUSTEO document, a 39-page briefing for Treasurer Peter Costello, said neighbouring New Zealand's defence spending was "inadequate" and detailed a cabinet strategy of Australian ministers pressing the need for bigger military spending on their Wellington counterparts at every opportunity.

Both AUSTEO documents were prepared for Costello for a summit of economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum in the tropical Australian resort town of Cairns earlier this month. AUSTEO is one of the highest security ratings.
The papers were among several left on a table in a public area at the hotel where the summit was held.
The second paper outlines Australian concern at New Zealand's defence budget.

"Inadequate NZ defence funding might mean Australia was seen to be accepting a disproportionate share of the bilateral burden," the paper said, adding that the latest draft of Wellington's upcoming defence review would still see long-term defence below 1990/91 levels.

The paper urges Costello to lobby New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters -- labelled an opportunist and loose cannon in the first paper -- on the need for Wellington to take more responsibility for defence.

"Raising Australia's concerns with Winston Peters...will register this message with the cabinet member who holds the 'purse-strings' over competing NZ budget priorities -- especially social policy versus defence interests," it said.
